children: Slovenia’s annual inflation rate edged up to 3.0% in August 2026, from 2.9% in July.
The acceleration was driven mainly by higher inflation in housing and utilities, which increased to 8.1% from 7.3%, and transport, which rose to 4.7% from 2.6%.
Inflation for insurance and financial services also accelerated, reaching 3.8% from 2.9%.

In contrast, price growth moderated for alcoholic beverages and tobacco (4.5% vs 4.7%), clothing and footwear (0.1% vs 0.9%), furnishings (0.7% vs 1.3%), health (1.5% vs 2.1%), information and communication (2.0% vs 2.8%), and recreation, sport and culture (5.3% vs 6.3%).
Food prices fell 1.0%, deepening from a 0.4% decline in July.
On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.1%, rebounding from a 0.1% decline in the previous month.

title: Slovenia Annual Inflation Edges Up
